data_section_full_text:
Our sample consists of post-Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) observations with available data for fiscal years 2004 to 2012. We
obtain auditor, internal control weakness, and restatement-related data from Audit Analytics, analyst data from the Institutional
Brokers’ Estimate System (I/B/E/S), and financial statement data from Compustat. We exclude all foreign incorporated and
financial services (two-digit SIC codes 60–69) observations from the sample. We also exclude observations with less than $5
million in total assets and all industry-years (based on two-digit SIC code) that contain fewer than ten observations to facilitate
calculation of abnormal accruals. After excluding observations without necessary data for variable calculation, our full sample
consists of 29,227 observations for auditor size and analyst following tests and 20,385 observations for internal control quality
tests. <sup>18</sup> Of these, 19,988 firm-years have a Big 4 auditor (BIG4it), 1,422 have at least one internal control weakness (WEAKit),
and 21,144 are followed by at least one analyst (ANALYSTit). Descriptive statistics for our full sample are presented in Table 2.

Research Design


We explore the effects of matching methods in three settings from accounting research: auditor size (BIG4it), internal
control quality (WEAKit), and analyst following (ANALYSTit). We use the following models to estimate propensity scores and
ATEs.
Prediction Model (first stage):

Equation (4) estimates the propensity to have the following treatments (Dit): BIG4it, WEAKit, or ANALYSTit. We match
observations on propensity score and impose a caliper distance of 0.03. Next, we estimate the ATE ðb <sup>^</sup> 1Þ on the matched sample
using Equation (5). We use abnormal accruals (ABSACCit) and generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) related
restatements (RESTATEit) to proxy for financial reporting quality (QUALITYit). Xit is a set of generic company-specific control
variables including: firm size (LNASSETSit), performance (ROAit and ATURNit), financial standing (CURRit, LEVit,

18 We use auditor-attested SOX 404 reports to capture internal control weaknesses (Skaife, Veenman, and Wangerin 2013). This constrains the sample to
company-years subject to SOX 404(b). We only include firms that are subject to SOX 404(b) to ensure that the process for identifying weaknesses is
the same for all sample firms. Also, we use the initial (i.e., non-restated) SOX 404 opinion to avoid a mechanical relation between restatements and
internal control weaknesses.
